name: parallel-plate-gap-3d
description: Closed form: t = sqrt(2 d m / (q E)) with E = V/gap. The corpus's first genuinely three-dimensional geometry - two square plates in a cubic box, which reduces to neither a cross-section nor an axis. Since the expected number is the same arithmetic the analytic accelerating-gap example uses, what is being checked here is the SOLVER: the field is computed rather than declared, and it reproduces 0.910572 us to a part in a million. Two things had to be right for that, and getting either wrong costs three orders of magnitude. The gap in the closed form is between the FACING SURFACES, so placing a 1 mm plate's centre on the gap boundary makes the real gap 9 mm and the field 11.111% high. And the applied voltage is split as plus and minus half rather than V and zero, because the grounded domain boundary is a third electrode: holding one plate at zero makes the boundary an extension of it, which is worth 0.31% of the field at the ends of the flight and 0.11% of the answer. Both figures are mesh-converged, so neither is a discretisation artefact that a finer grid would remove.
